name: Substitution
overview: The Scriptures reveal the principle of substitution as a divine provision for atonement and consecration, where one party bears the iniquity or consequence of another. Aaron, as the high priest, symbolically carries the iniquity of the holy offerings on his forehead to ensure their acceptance before the LORD, demonstrating a personal identification with the people's sin (Exodus 28:38). The burnt offering and the scapegoat rituals further illustrate this, with the offerer placing hands on the sacrifice to transfer guilt and the live goat bearing Israel's sins into the wilderness, signifying removal of iniquity (Leviticus 1:4; 16:21-22). Additionally, the Levites are chosen by God to stand in place of the firstborn among Israel, highlighting substitution in service and dedication to the LORD (Numbers 3:12, 3:41). These examples collectively underscore substitution as a foundational biblical motif where life, guilt, or service is transferred to fulfill God's requirements and maintain covenant relationship.
